title: Leek and sweetcorn fritters with tomatoes

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain kitchen staple: leeks, corn, flour, eggs, milk, cheddar, tomatoes, yoghurt and chives.

supermarket.reason: Everything is an everyday item at Tesco, and corn cobs are cheap and easy to find in October.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, bowl, whisk and grater, and shallow-frying spoonfuls of batter is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 150g self-raising flour with 2 eggs and 150ml milk makes a sensible thick batter for two leeks, two cobs and 75g cheddar, giving about 12 fritters for four, with seasoning and timings that hold up.

honest_times.reason: The 10 cook minutes cannot cover the 8 minutes softening the leeks, the fritters fried at 3 minutes a side (which for four means two or three batches, roughly 15 to 18 minutes at the stove) and the 3 minutes for the tomatoes, so the real hands-on time runs well past the 40 minutes printed in total.

honest_ingredients.reason: 'Corn cobs' is the same food as sweetcorn, and every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, with nothing unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: Leeks are central to a warm fritter breakfast that suits a cool October morning, alongside the last of the corn and tomatoes.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in British English, and nothing in them would confuse a beginner.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling breakfast of vegetables, eggs, cheese and yoghurt that a family would happily eat again.
